Time to get hands-on! The goal of these exercises is that prepare-draw-flip-wait stops feeling like a recipe you follow and starts feeling like something you *do*.

Work in a new script, `playground.py`, and **run after every part**.

### Part 1 · Flip a coloured window

Open a window with any background colour you like (`'black'`, `'grey'`, `'pink'`, `'darkblue'`...), make the colour actually appear, hold it for two seconds, and close cleanly. 

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core

win = visual.Window(size=(1280, 720), fullscr=False,
                    color='darkblue', checkTiming=False)
win.flip()      # paint the background — no flip, no colour!
core.wait(2)
win.close()
core.quit()
```
:::

::::

### Part 2 · Prepare and draw text

Before the wait: prepare a `TextStim` with your own name, draw it, flip. Experiment with `height` (try 0.05 against 0.2) and `color` until it stands out against your background.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
name = visual.TextStim(win, text='Chris was here!',
                       color='orange', height=0.15)
name.draw()
win.flip()
core.wait(2)
```
:::

### Part 3 · Two draws, one flip

The back buffer is a stage you can keep arranging before the curtain rises. Draw the rabbit **and** your name, then flip once: both appear together, in a single instant. Try it: rabbit in the centre, your name above it (give the `TextStim` a position, for example `pos=(0, 0.7)`).

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core

win = visual.Window(size=(1280, 720), fullscr=False,
                    color='black', checkTiming=False)

pic = visual.ImageStim(win, image='rabbit.jpg')
label = visual.TextStim(win, text='My rabbit', color='white',
                        height=0.08, pos=(0, 0.7))

pic.draw()       # backstage: rabbit first...
label.draw()     # ...label after, so it sits on top
win.flip()       # one flip reveals both
event.waitKeys()

win.close()
core.quit()
```
:::

::::

:::: {.content-visible unless-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

### Part 4 · A full sequence

Now chain the parts into one script: your name for two seconds, then the labelled rabbit until a keypress, then close. One prepare, draw, flip, wait per screen.

:::: {.content-visible when-meta="show-solutions-s2"}

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show the code"}
```python
from psychopy import visual, event, core

win = visual.Window(size=(1280, 720), fullscr=False,
                    color='darkblue', checkTiming=False)

name = visual.TextStim(win, text='Anna was here!',
                       color='orange', height=0.15)
name.draw()
win.flip()
core.wait(2)

pic = visual.ImageStim(win, image='rabbit.jpg')
label = visual.TextStim(win, text='My rabbit', color='white',
                        height=0.08, pos=(0, 0.7))
pic.draw()
label.draw()
win.flip()
event.waitKeys()

win.close()
core.quit()
```
:::
